caption: The video captures a hiker in a cap, jacket and large backpack standing on a dark rocky ledge at the right edge of a river canyon, head bowed toward their hands. A wide, muddy river churns through the canyon toward a distant waterfall whose spray forms a drifting white mist plume, while a low columnar rock cliff lines the left bank beneath a sky thick with white and grey clouds. An out-of-focus grass stem and pale leafy bushes occupy the immediate foreground. The hiker's posture shifts subtly across the clip, the bowed head remaining largely consistent as the arms and hands move slightly relative to the torso. The blurred foreground stem drifts steadily across the frame, the river surface shows continuous turbulent flow with changing ripples, and the waterfall mist plume drifts and reshapes. The cloud cover reorganizes slowly overhead, and the camera drifts slightly, causing the scene elements to shift leftward within the frame. The visible process continues without resolution.

endpoints are normal, not physical errors. Do not add unseen causes, onset, stopping or outcomes.
An internal editing cut is not evidence of physical motion connecting the views.

Check identification before physical interpretation: a reflection is not a separate actor;
a powder/smoke/liquid outline or shadow is not automatically the boundary of a solid object;
an apparent change caused by occlusion/viewpoint is not automatically material deformation.
Do not claim contact, bending, compression, melting, disintegration or structural recovery unless
the appropriate material/surface itself provides visible evidence. Do not infer a force or earlier
collision just because the visible configuration would be compatible with it.
Compare several frames before asserting translation, rotation, direction, unchanged position or
camera tracking. A single visible texture/seam does not prove spin. Avoid unnecessary absolute
claims of stillness, no motion, no camera motion or 'exactly' synchronized changes.
Remove invented scene details and explanations, but keep clearly visible ongoing motion and
processes. Avoid deleting the real process merely because its cause lies outside the cropped window.

Retain the WISA English narrative style, detail density and paragraph structure. Aim for the
provided original word count within 85%-115%, using genuinely visible details and process.
Do not add repetition, watermark/logo descriptions or atmospheric filler to reach a word count.

'this mid-segment', 'the excerpt', 'the frame', 'these images', 'observed evidence' in the caption.
This is a direct video description, not an analysis note. No mandatory beginning/end formula.
Complete every sentence. If accuracy requires a substantial length difference, explain it outside

draft_caption: The video captures a hiker in a cap, jacket and large backpack standing on a dark rocky ledge at the right edge of a river canyon, head bowed toward their hands. A wide, muddy river churns through the canyon toward a distant waterfall whose spray forms a drifting white mist plume, while a low columnar rock cliff lines the left bank beneath a sky thick with white and grey clouds. An out-of-focus grass stem and pale leafy bushes occupy the immediate foreground. The hiker's posture shifts subtly across the clip, the bowed head rising a little as the cap brim rotates from pointing down-left toward a more horizontal forward orientation, while the arms and hands move slightly relative to the torso. The blurred foreground stem sways left and right in the wind, the river surface shows continuous turbulent flow with changing ripples, and the waterfall mist plume drifts and reshapes. The cloud cover reorganizes slowly overhead, and the camera stays fixed on the scene with minor handheld wobble. The visible process continues without resolution.
